description: A clock divider giving every power of two from 2 to 256 alongside thirds, fifths and sevenths and their halves

inputs.text: Drives the eight power-of-two outputs on each rise above 1V, and feeds the other three clock inputs whenever they are empty
Clocks the 3 and 3/2 outputs; with nothing patched it takes the clock from the main input at the bottom
Clocks the 5 and 5/2 outputs; with nothing patched it takes the clock from the main input at the bottom
Clocks the 7 and 7/2 outputs; with nothing patched it takes the clock from the main input at the bottom

outputs.text: A gate at 5V for one clock and 0V for the next
A gate at 5V for two clocks and 0V for the next two
A gate at 5V for four clocks and 0V for the next four
A gate at 5V for eight clocks and 0V for the next eight
A gate at 5V for sixteen clocks and 0V for the next sixteen
A gate at 5V for thirty-two clocks and 0V for the next thirty-two
A gate at 5V for sixty-four clocks and 0V for the next sixty-four
A gate at 5V for one hundred and twenty-eight clocks and 0V for the next hundred and twenty-eight
A square wave at one third the rate of the clock on that row
A square wave at two thirds the rate of the clock on that row, changing state on the clock's falling edge as well as its rising edge
A square wave at one fifth the rate of the clock on that row
A square wave at two fifths the rate of the clock on that row, changing state on the clock's falling edge as well as its rising edge
A square wave at one seventh the rate of the clock on that row
A square wave at two sevenths the rate of the clock on that row, changing state on the clock's falling edge as well as its rising edge

notes: the three upper clock inputs are normalled to the main input at the bottom, so one cable there runs all fourteen outputs.
to reach a division the panel does not print, patch one output back into one of the clock inputs: the /2 output into the 7 row's clock input gives a division by 14 at the 7 output.
